propositions.text: The appellant is a citizen of India fearing police persecution if returned.
propositions.quote: The appellant, XXXX XXXX, is a citizen of India. He is alleging that he fears returning to his country because he is afraid that the police will go after him again.

propositions.text: Appellant married a woman in 2009 who was involved with another man; she returned to her family.
propositions.quote: On XXXX XXXX, 2009, the appellant allegedly married a woman who was in a relationship with another man. His wife supposedly returned to live with her family.

propositions.text: Police sided with wife's uncle to get appellant to pay for divorce; appellant's family paid and police tortured his father.
propositions.quote: The police apparently sided with his wife's uncle to get him to pay money for a divorce. The appellant's family allegedly paid for his divorce and the police tortured his father.

propositions.text: Police and wife's uncle falsely accused appellant of helping activists, attributing political opinion to him.
propositions.quote: The police and his wife's uncle reportedly falsely accused the appellant of helping activists, thereby attributing a political opinion to him.

propositions.text: Police arrested and tortured appellant twice; he fled to Switzerland then came to Canada in 2013.
propositions.quote: The police apparently arrested and tortured the appellant twice. Once released, the appellant reportedly fled to Switzerland before coming to Canada on XXXX XXXX, 2013.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant alleges fearing police persecution in India due to family and political accusations, fleeing to Switzerland then Canada in 2013.

propositions.text: Minister's representative asks RPD to reject claim due to credibility issues and delay in seeking protection.
propositions.quote: The representative of the Minister of Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship intervened in this case, asking the Refugee Protection Division (RPD) to reject the appellant's refugee protection claim because of the credibility issues noted in his written account. He pointed out the appellant's delay in seeking Canada's protection, which demonstrates a lack of subjective fear.

paragraphs.summary: Minister's representative argues for rejection due to credibility problems and delay in seeking protection.

propositions.text: RPD rejected appellant's claim for lack of credibility due to contradictions and lack of subjective fear.
propositions.quote: On November 1, 2019, the RPD rejected the appellant's refugee protection claim, finding that he was not a credible witness because of contradictions in his testimony and behaviour, which demonstrates a lack of subjective fear in India.

paragraphs.summary: RPD rejected claim for credibility contradictions and lack of subjective fear.

propositions.text: Appellant argues RPD failed to analyze claim under section 96 IRPA.
propositions.quote: He is arguing that the RPD failed to analyze his refugee protection claim under section 96 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act1 (IRPA).

propositions.text: Appellant alleges RPD breached natural justice by disregarding much evidence presented.
propositions.quote: The appellant is also arguing that the RPD breached the principles of natural justice and procedural fairness by disregarding much of the evidence that he presented.

propositions.text: Appellant alleges RPD erred in credibility assessment; contradictions minor and delay not determinative.
propositions.quote: The appellant is also alleging that the RPD erred in its assessment of his credibility since the contradictions identified are minor and his delay in claiming refugee protection is not a determinative factor.

propositions.text: Appellant argues RPD erred in failing to analyze internal flight alternative (IFA).
propositions.quote: In addition, the appellant is also arguing that the RPD erred in failing to analyze an internal flight alternative (IFA).

paragraphs.summary: Appellant argues RPD erred on section 96 analysis, natural justice, credibility, and internal flight alternative.

propositions.text: Determinative issue is whether RPD breached natural justice and erred in credibility assessment.
propositions.quote: In my view, the determinative issue for the Refugee Appeal Division (RAD) is whether the RPD breached the principles of natural justice and procedural fairness and whether it erred in its assessment of the appellant's credibility.

propositions.text: After independent analysis, RPD decision was incorrect.
propositions.quote: After conducting a complete and independent analysis of the evidence presented, I conclude that the RPD decision was incorrect.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds key issue is natural justice breach and credibility error; concludes RPD decision was incorrect.

propositions.text: Appeal is allowed and matter referred to differently constituted RPD panel.
propositions.quote: The appeal is allowed. I refer the matter to a differently constituted RPD panel.

paragraphs.summary: Appeal allowed; case referred to new RPD panel.

propositions.text: RAD applies correctness standard per Huruglica, except where RPD has advantage in credibility assessment.
propositions.quote: The RAD must apply the standard of correctness in accordance with the Federal Court of Appeal's decision in Huruglica. The exception to this rule is where the RPD enjoys a meaningful advantage in assessing credibility.

propositions.text: RPD did not have particular advantage in assessing credibility in this case.
propositions.quote: In my view, the RPD did not enjoy any particular advantage in this case.

paragraphs.summary: Court states RAD applies correctness standard; RPD had no advantage in credibility here.

propositions.text: Court will conduct own analysis including hearing recording, applying correctness standard.
propositions.quote: As a result, I will conduct my own analysis of the record, which includes listening to the recording of the hearing, to establish whether the RPD erred, applying the correctness standard of review.

paragraphs.summary: Court will independently analyze record and hearing recording applying correctness standard.

propositions.text: Appellant argues RPD failed to analyze claim under section 96 IRPA.
propositions.quote: The appellant is arguing that the RPD failed to analyze his refugee protection claim under section 96 of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: Appellant argues RPD failed to analyze claim under section 96 IRPA.

propositions.text: Negative credibility finding may be determinative under section 96 but not necessarily under section 97 IRPA.
propositions.quote: although a negative credibility finding may be determinative in the case of a refugee protection claim under section 96 of the IRPA, that is not necessarily so in the case of a refugee protection claim under section 97.

propositions.text: Appellant's criticism that RPD failed section 96 analysis is unfounded in this case.
propositions.quote: with all due respect to the appellant, I am of the opinion that, in this case, this criticism is unfounded for the following reasons.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds negative credibility may be determinative under section 96 but appellant's criticism is unfounded here.

propositions.text: RPD stated claim concerns fear of persecution based on imputed political opinion.
propositions.quote: the RPD clearly states at the outset of its decision that the refugee protection claim concerns an alleged fear of persecution based on an imputed political opinion.

propositions.text: RPD rejected claim due to lack of credibility and disbelief of appellant's events.
propositions.quote: the RPD rejected the appellant's refugee protection claim essentially because it found that he was not a credible witness and it did not believe the events alleged by the appellant.

propositions.text: RPD's conclusion applies to both section 96 and 97 analyses; appellant is neither Convention refugee nor person in need of protection.
propositions.quote: Ultimately, the RPD concluded that the appellant is neither a "Convention refugee" under section 96 of the IRPA nor a "person in need of protection" under subsection 97(1).

paragraphs.summary: Court finds RPD analyzed claim under section 96 and 97, rejecting appellant as neither refugee nor person in need of protection.

propositions.text: RPD did analyze appellant's refugee protection claim under section 96 IRPA.
propositions.quote: I am of the opinion that the RPD did indeed analyze the appellant's refugee protection claim under section 96 of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: Court concludes RPD analyzed claim under section 96 IRPA.

propositions.text: Appellant alleges RPD breached natural justice and procedural fairness by disregarding much evidence.
propositions.quote: The appellant alleges that the RPD breached the principles of natural justice and procedural fairness by disregarding much of the evidence that he presented.

paragraphs.summary: Appellant alleges RPD breached natural justice by disregarding much evidence.

propositions.text: More relevant evidence must be mentioned in reasons; dismissing evidence requires sound articulated reason.
propositions.quote: it is generally understood that the more relevant the evidence, the more important it is to mention it in the reasons. Moreover, there must be a sound and articulated reason for dismissing a refugee protection claimant's evidence as self-serving.

paragraphs.summary: Court states relevant evidence must be mentioned and dismissal requires sound reasons.

propositions.text: Appellant submitted affidavits from brother, friend, father, and sarpanch as evidence.
propositions.quote: the appellant submitted several pieces of personal evidence in support of his claims, namely, exhibits C-4 to C-7. These consist of affidavits from his brother, a friend, his father and a sarpanch.

propositions.text: RPD gave no probative value to affidavits except father's due to inconsistencies and self-serving nature.
propositions.quote: The RPD's comments come down to the RPD not giving any probative value to the documents submitted, with the exception of Exhibit C-6, his father's affidavit, because there are inconsistencies in each of the documents and because the RPD considered them to be self-serving.

paragraphs.summary: Appellant submitted affidavits; RPD rejected most as inconsistent and self-serving except father's affidavit.

propositions.text: RPD did not explain how affidavits were unsatisfactory or note appellant's explanations; hearing record shows no questioning on this evidence.
propositions.quote: it is not clear from these comments exactly how the documents were unsatisfactory, what inconsistencies were noted by the RPD, or what the appellant's explanations were for those inconsistencies. In fact, the recording of the hearing reveals that the RPD did not question the appellant about this evidence.

propositions.text: RPD should have obtained and assessed appellant's explanations for inconsistencies in evidence.
propositions.quote: Consequently, the RPD's decision does not mention that it obtained and assessed the appellant's responses to determine whether or not his explanations for the inconsistencies noted were satisfactory. This should have been done, as this evidence directly relates to the main allegations of the appellant's refugee protection claim.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds RPD failed to explain rejection of affidavits or question appellant on inconsistencies, which it should have done.

propositions.text: RPD erred significantly in disregarding evidence without sufficient reasons.
propositions.quote: I conclude that the RPD did indeed err significantly in disregarding this evidence without providing sufficient reasons.

propositions.text: Court cannot remedy error without oral hearing; refers case for re-examination of evidence including affidavits and testimony.
propositions.quote: It is impossible for me to remedy this error by confirming, setting aside its determination and substituting a determination that, in my opinion, should have been made without holding an oral hearing in order to re-examine the evidence, particularly exhibits C-4 to C-7 that were presented to the RPD, including the appellant's testimony.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds RPD erred in disregarding evidence without reasons and refers case for re-examination with oral hearing.

propositions.text: Matter referred to differently constituted RPD panel for re-determination.
propositions.quote: Consequently, I refer the matter to a differently constituted RPD panel for re-determination.

paragraphs.summary: Court refers matter to new RPD panel for re-determination.

propositions.text: No need to address appellant's claims on minor contradictions and delay given natural justice conclusion; new panel will assess credibility.
propositions.quote: As for the appellant's claims that the RPD considered minor contradictions and his delay in claiming refugee protection in Canada to find that he was not credible, I do not consider that I need to address this on appeal, given my earlier conclusion regarding natural justice. The differently constituted panel will be able to assess the appellant's credibility.

paragraphs.summary: Court declines to address minor contradictions and delay claims; new panel will assess credibility.

propositions.text: RPD did not err in failing to analyze internal flight alternative because it found appellant not credible.
propositions.quote: with respect to the appellant's claim on appeal that the RPD erred in failing to analyze an IFA, suffice it to say that it was not necessary for the RPD to do so because it did not find the appellant credible with respect to the allegations forming the basis of his refugee protection claim.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds RPD did not err in not analyzing internal flight alternative due to appellant's lack of credibility.

propositions.text: The appeal is allowed.
propositions.quote: The appeal is allowed.

propositions.text: The matter is referred to a differently constituted RPD panel.
propositions.quote: I refer the matter to a differently constituted RPD panel.

paragraphs.summary: The court allows the appeal and refers the matter to a differently constituted RPD panel.
